title: Treviño Answers Questions Alone as Cigarroa Skips City Runoff Forum

content:
Mayor Victor Treviño answered questions alone at a mayoral runoff forum Wednesday night, after challenger Alyssa Cigarroa withdrew — leaving the Nov. 18 event at Laredo City Hall a one-candidate affair less than a month before the Dec. 12 runoff.

The forum was part of the city's Laredo Votes 2026 voter-education campaign. Univision and Fox Laredo reporter Miriam Salinas put six questions to Treviño.

Cigarroa, the District VIII councilmember, told the city on Tuesday that she would stay away, saying officials had favored the mayor, including in how they promoted him online. City officials replied that the participation rules were explained at required orientations and applied the same way to every candidate in the series.

Cigarroa also did not attend an Oct. 8 city forum, which the Public Information Office attributed to a scheduling conflict. She has taken part in events hosted by the Kiwanis Club of Laredo and Texas A&M International University.

What Treviño said

On downtown, Treviño said the area needs incentives for property owners and merchants, along with a review of the tax programs now in place. On water, he said roughly 40,000 feet of old line has been swapped out for about $130 million, and he described plans to divide the system into four zones so a break would not force a boil-water notice across the whole city. He also mentioned a city app under development that would let residents track water breaks and estimated repair times.

Asked about options once Bethany House runs out of space, the mayor replied that homelessness stems from varied causes and calls for individual solutions, depending on whether a person is struggling mentally, physically or financially. He also backed widening the World Trade Bridge and improving other border crossings, noting the volume of freight that moves through Laredo.

In his closing remarks, he named honesty, diplomacy, schooling and experience as what a mayor needs, and said the job means being on hand when conditions are hard.

After the forum

Treviño told reporters afterward that Cigarroa's absence disappointed him. “This should have been a debate, and my opponent did not show up,” he said. Cigarroa has said staying away does not signal a retreat from the public and that she is reaching residents in other ways.

Where the race stands

The two finished first and second in the five-person Nov. 3 race, with Cigarroa taking 35.54% to Treviño's 32.29% — a 1,785-vote difference in unofficial results. The runoff is Dec. 12. Both candidates are expected at a Laredo Chamber of Commerce forum Dec. 8.

What to watch now: whether Cigarroa attends the Dec. 8 forum, and whether the city's forum rules become a campaign issue in the final weeks of the runoff.

Update — November 25, 2026: The Laredo Chamber of Commerce moved its mayoral runoff forum to Wednesday, December 2, at 6:30 p.m., airing live on KGNS-TV 8 and KGNS+. It had originally been scheduled for December 8, the last day of early voting. Both candidates are expected to take part.

Update — November 26, 2026: Laredo City Councilmember Dr. Tyler King, who represents District 6, endorsed Alyssa Cigarroa for mayor in a video posted November 23, 2026, on his own Facebook page and Instagram account. In the video, filmed at Veterans Memorial Central Park, King said it would be easy to stay on the sidelines but that the election is too important, framing the choice as between “business as usual” and a new direction for Laredo, and said he was proud to endorse his “dear friend.” He noted that Cigarroa gave up the last two years of her city council seat to run for mayor because “things are too dire right now to wait four more years.” The video, a political advertisement paid for by Ricardo A. Sandoval, Treasurer, closes with early voting November 30 through December 8 and Election Day December 12.
